title: Solo developers, multiplayer and stores with persistent items
author: FlashMcSuave
selftext:
I am working on a long term project which involves live PVP multiplayer as well as a store with persistent items. 

My assumption has been that I need to develop a project that doesn't yet bring in multiplayer and the store, and those aspects can come later after I have other partners. As such I have been designing the game with multiplayer in mind, with key match-outcome variables sitting in the core while visuals and so on are handled locally. 

My assumption about needing other partners rests on the following:

\- live PVP Multiplayer can't have lag. This isn't turn based. I would need server specialists. This could possibly be overcome by a single developer though?

\- An Online store with real money means persistent identifiers for all players as well as items, to prevent cheaters duping. 

\- This online store would also mean support chat options and refunds and so on.

\- Live chat and other multiplayer aspects would also need a degree of monitoring to ensure there isn't inappropriate behaviour. 

Are my assumptions correct? Has anyone else here worked on a project with these elements? What kind of partners are needed? Are there other hazards I need to be aware of?

comments.author: Kingnorik
comments.body: Make a game then worry about monetization. There are already services you pay for it that would handle things like support.

comments.author: puzzles-errday
comments.body:
Things like servers for running live pvp are essentially a solved problem. You won’t see professional companies reinventing the wheel here, and you don’t have to worry so strongly about it for your personal project. Claude can certainly help with this.

However, where you’re wrong is that developing with pvp in mind can wait until later. That should almost certainly be part of the development process early on, because it will affect your architecture for all facets of the game’s code - both on the server and the client. I’d start getting on that immediately if that is a requirement for you.

replies.author: FlashMcSuave
replies.body:
Yup - I am designing it with multiplayer in mind from the beginning with all the architecture.

My main concern is around the demands on item tracking and user profiles - and preventing people from duplicating items or hacking characters, etc. I would have thought that this requires more infrastructure - also human infrastructure for managing it all as most games of this nature are by studios. 

But I do recognise that this is a good problem to have if the game is indeed popular - but I have an online store and items as the final piece of the roadmap so I want to ensure that from the beginning it is designed in a way where I can quickly pivot to accommodate that.

replies.author: puzzles-errday
replies.body: Yep, all of that requires infrastructure. One way you can deal with it easily right now is to use a "backend as a service". Something like Braincloud, which lets you set up item tracking, currencies, user data, etc., without needing to go into something like AWS to handle it all yourself. A lot of the scaffolding is provided for you automatically. Just some food for thought in case you haven't considered that option.
